text: Students came from across Asia to study at Nalanda,
one of the world's earliest great universities.
With thousands of students and a library so big,
it filled several buildings.
Even the iron got better.
The iron pillar of Delhi, made in the Gupta Age,
has stood in the open for about 1,600 years,
and has barely rusted.
My bicycle rusted in one monsoon.
But in the 500s, raiders called the Hunas swept in from Central Asia.
The Gupta Empire cracked, shattered.
Again.
In the south, though, the story was just getting started.
The Chola Kings of Tamil Nadu built one of the greatest navies in Asian history.
Rajaraja I built the vast Brihadishwarar temple at Tangivore, finished around 1010.
Its tower is about 66 meters tall.
His son, Rajendra, sent his fleet across the Bay of Bengal to attack the mighty Srivijaya
Kingdom in Sumatra and Malaya.
Hmm, an Indian navy?
Waiting Southeast Asia?
A thousand years ago?
But in the north, things were about to change.
A powerful sultan had just learned how rich India's temples were.
